title: Generic base change for a smooth morphism with finite locally constant coefficients (finite ring)
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $k$ be a field, $S$ an integral scheme of finite type over $k$ on which the exponent of $\Lambda$ is invertible, $a\colon X\to S$ a separated, quasi-compact, smooth morphism, and $F$ a finite locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-constructible-locally-constant]. Then there is a nonempty open $U\subseteq S$ such that $Ra_{U,*}(F|_{X_U})$ is bounded with constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and for every morphism $v\colon T\to U$ from a Noetherian scheme the base change map $v^*Ra_{U,*}(F|_{X_U})\to Ra_{T,*}(F|_{X_T})$ [sbc-def-base-change-map] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a positive integer n annihilating the finite coefficient ring and invertible on S. Prove the assertion for any finite locally constant sheaf annihilated by such an n, by strong induction on n. If n=1 the sheaf is zero and U=S works. Otherwise write n=p*m with p prime. Then 0<m<n and both p and m are invertible on S. Since S is nonempty, p differs from char(k): otherwise p is zero in the global sections, contradicting invertibility after passage to any stalk. Smoothness supplies local finite type for the prime-field theorem.

source.place: Finite coefficient devissage; elementary induction on a positive annihilator

proof.text: Let K be the kernel of p acting on F and Q the cokernel of K -> F. These are finite locally constant by the kernel and cokernel closure. K is killed by p. Q is the coimage of multiplication by p, so m kills Q because m*p kills F. This gives the short exact sequence 0 -> K -> F -> Q -> 0. Lift the underlying abelian sheaf of K to an actual ULift(ZMod p)-module sheaf H using the sectionwise killed-sheaf construction. The underlying-sheaf isomorphism transfers finite local constancy to H.

source.place: Finite torsion devissage, with kernels and coimages rather than an explicit prime-factor filtration

proof.text: Apply the prime-field smooth generic theorem to H. On its nonempty open U the unbounded derived direct image is bounded with finite locally constant cohomology. Convert to the bounded-below model by the upper-star and right-derived comparison isomorphisms. For a noetherian test square with image in U, its lower-left scheme is isomorphic to the noetherian test scheme, so is noetherian. Factor its map to S through U. Pullback preserves bounded constructibility, and the prime-field exchange identifies this pullback with the required test direct image. Paste with the open restriction square, whose exchange is invertible, to obtain precisely the exchange for the original square over S.

source.place: Smooth generic theorem; open restriction and horizontal exchange pasting

proof.text: Transfer this property from H to K through the isomorphism of their underlying abelian sheaves. The canonical coefficient comparisons identify the derived pullbacks, direct images and exchanges for both rings. Their homology comparisons identify underlying abelian cohomology sheaves. On each constructibility stratum finite local constancy transfers through the same underlying-sheaf isomorphism; vanishing is reflected by the faithful forgetful functor. Exchange compatibility identifies the forgotten exchange with the abelian exchange, and forgetting reflects its invertibility by the cohomology criterion. Thus K has the full required property on U.

source.place: Coefficient-independent direct image and exchange, with constructibility checked on strata

proof.text: The induction hypothesis for m and Q gives a nonempty open V. Since S is integral, U intersect V is nonempty. Restrict both properties to the intersection by monotonicity of the allowed image set. The short exact sequence K -> F -> Q supplies a distinguished triangle of degree-zero bounded-below complexes. Apply HasDirectImageBaseChangeOnPlus.of_distTriang2: derived direct image of pullback preserves distinguished triangles, bounded constructibility is triangulated, and the exchange is a morphism of triangles, so invertibility at the first and third terms implies invertibility at the second. This proves the property for F and completes induction. Finally apply the induction to the ring annihilator, which annihilates every section of F.
